Mac Catalyst / Designed for iPad vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Mac availability workflow covers language. Connect and Xcode actually separate Mac distribution from storefront copy:

  • Mac Catalyst / Designed for iPad — controls whether your iPad app runs on macOS and appears on the Mac App Store. Xcode project settings, entitlements, and Mac build submission — engineering, not listing copy.
  • Mac binary packaging and notarization — signing, archiving, and submitting the macOS build. Distribution engineering — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Mac availability badges on the product page — Apple may render "Also available on Mac" or "Designed for iPad" chrome from your Connect configuration. Badge chrome may localize; your name, subtitle, description, and screenshot overlays do not unless you fill zh-Hans fields.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store (iOS and Mac). Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines on both iOS and Mac product pages. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Mac Catalyst flags.

A compliant US listing with Mac Catalyst enabled and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Mac-curious purchasers browsing the China App Store on iPhone, iPad, or Mac evaluate iPad-on-Mac value in the first scroll. Common failure modes when only en-US is filled:

Better zh-Hans listing copy helps Mac-curious buyers understand iPad-on-Mac availability before install. It does not replace Mac Catalyst configuration, Mac build submission, notarization, or Apple's review decisions.

Mac Catalyst–specific listing copy — what translates differently

iPad-on-Mac listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Mac availability — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Designed for iPad vs Also available on Mac

US pages use "Designed for iPad", "Also available on Mac", or "Mac Catalyst." China storefront copy often uses 专为iPad设计, 也可在Mac上使用, Mac版, or Mac Catalyst — depending on whether you mean Apple's Designed for iPad badge, Catalyst distribution, or a generic Mac promise. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual Mac distribution setup, not inventing Mac support your app does not ship.

Optimized for Mac phrasing

Some listings claim "Optimized for Mac" when the app adapts keyboard, menu bar, or window chrome for macOS. Chinese buyers expect concrete Mac value (Mac优化, 键盘快捷键, 菜单栏) rather than English slogans ("Feels at home on Mac") that hide whether the app is a direct iPad port or a Mac-adapted experience.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Mac-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like Mac版, iPad版, and 跨平台 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Also available on Mac" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Common mistakes on Mac Catalyst zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Mac Catalyst localizes automatically — Catalyst enabled and Mac build submitted; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US Mac badges verbatim — Latin "Designed for iPad" badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Conflating listing copy with Catalyst engineering — description explains how to enable Mac Catalyst in Xcode instead of what the buyer gets; setup instructions belong in support docs, not AppLocale scope
  • Mixing up this page with per-device Mac screenshot work — Mac desktop gallery captions localized but Mac availability story still English on subtitle and description; or the reverse
  • Mixing up Mac Catalyst with Universal Purchase — cross-platform purchase badges localized but Designed for iPad availability copy still English; or Catalyst marketing pasted where Universal Purchase copy belongs
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Expecting AppLocale to enable Mac Catalyst — Catalyst entitlements, AppKit code, notarization, and Mac binary packaging are outside listing rewrite

FAQ

Does enabling Mac Catalyst or Designed for iPad auto-translate my China listing?

No. Mac Catalyst and Designed for iPad control Mac distribution — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback on iOS and Mac storefronts.

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines — rewritten from your English Mac availability listing originals.

Can AppLocale configure Mac Catalyst, AppKit, or Mac binary packaging?

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. Catalyst entitlements, AppKit code, notarization, and Mac build submission are outside AppLocale scope.

How is this different from iPad, Mac, or Watch screenshot guides?

This page covers the Mac availability story on shared listing fields — "Designed for iPad" and "Also available on Mac" marketing. Per-device screenshot sets are separate Connect upload matrices for when buyers browse on Mac desktop hardware.

How is this different from Universal Purchase listing copy?

Universal Purchase covers one-purchase-across-all-platforms marketing — "Buy once, use on all your devices." Mac Catalyst copy covers iPad-on-Mac availability — "Designed for iPad" and "Also available on Mac" — even when purchases are separate per platform.

Why do screenshot captions still say "Designed for iPad" in English on China?

Caption and overlay fields are managed per localization. If you filled en-US screenshot text but never saved zh-Hans caption lines — or uploaded the same English-overlay PNGs to the Chinese set — China buyers see Latin Mac availability badges on the product page.
